speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have a pruritic rash on your trunk and extremities along with a low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. To narrow this down, have you noticed if the rash blanches (turns white) when you press on it, or if it appears to be spreading to your palms or soles?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: That facial rash sparing the area around your mouth is a key clue; were your joints stiff in the morning, and did you experience any eye redness or pain? REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC) with differential.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pyelonephritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
I must correct the previous physician's assessment; Pyelonephritis is a kidney infection and does not present with the rash or respiratory symptoms you are describing. Please confirm if the facial rash you mentioned is a "slapped cheek" appearance, and have you noticed any red lines on your hands or feet?

REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC) with differential.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease)
